test_title: SSC Stenographer 2025 Official Paper (Held On: 07 Aug, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
Arrange the sentence parts:

(A) on time

(B) the bus

(C) arrived

(D) at the stop
solution:
The correct answer is **Option (1)** i.e. **BCAD**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The logical order of the sentence starts with the subject "**the bus**" – indicated by **(B)**.
 
• Next comes the verb "**arrived**" – indicated by **(C)**, showing the action done by the bus.
 
• The phrase "on time" – indicated by (A), specifies when it happened.
 
• Finally, indicated by "at the stop" – (D), tells where the bus arrived. completing the sentence meaningfully.

Therefore, the correct answer is **BCAD.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2 (BACD):** Incorrect because “the bus on time arrived at the stop” is grammatically wrong – the adverbial phrase “on time” should come at the end.
 
• **Option 3 (CBAD):** Incorrect as “arrived the bus on time at the stop” does not follow subject–verb order.
 
• **Option 4 (ABCD):** Incorrect because “on time the bus arrived at the stop” is awkward and not a natural English structure.
